facts.text: Oakwood’s Schantz Park neighborhood, with 400 homes, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and showcases turn‑of‑the‑century architectural styles.
The Long‑Romspert Homestead, a living history museum, lets visitors step into everyday American life from the 1800s to today.
Orville Wright’s Oakwood home, Hawthorn Hill, is part of the National Aviation Heritage Area that honors the Dayton region as the birthplace of powered flight.
Oakwood hosted the first Soap Box Derby, a milestone that sparked a national tradition of youth racing.
The city’s Boy Scouts Troop 101 was one of the first chartered by the BSA, and the blue and gold Cub Scout uniform colors were inspired by Oakwood High School’s team colors.
Every spring, the Oakwood Historical Society opens the Long‑Romspert Homestead for house museum tours, offering a glimpse into the town’s rich past.
